title: A Christmas Carol Stretch
welcome_lead: Stretch: is Scrooge's transformation convincing or convenient? Build the essay.
meta_desc: GCSE English Literature — essay-level evaluation of A Christmas Carol's redemption arc.
final_note: You evaluated Scrooge's redemption as theological, structural and political — and the novella as a 'sledgehammer blow'.

concepts.def: Economic system based on private profit
Strong argument against an opposing view

walkthroughs.body_html:
Scrooge sees his own grave (a memento mori) and 'wakes' on Christmas morning — a kind of resurrection.

Dickens deliberately echoes the gospel pattern: death of the old self, birth of the new. Redemption isn't just psychological — it's spiritual.

Some critics call Scrooge's overnight change unrealistic.

But Dickens is writing a didactic ghost story, not a realist novel. Each ghost dismantles a specific defence: 'I never knew' (Past), 'I never cared' (Present), 'It won't matter' (Future). Each is answered.

The novella is a polemic against laissez-faire capitalism dressed as a feel-good story.

Scrooge raises Bob's wages — but Dickens wants every employer in his readership to do the same. The 'sledgehammer blow' lands when the reader becomes Scrooge.
